resources.string: A direct connection to your machine: no relay, no server in between. The first time, get on the same WiFi as the PC and scan its QR. After that it does not matter where you are: the link does not expire, you only need to be able to reach the machine — same network, or your VPN. If the address changes, correct it here; there is no need to pair again.
Point at the QR the machine is showing
That QR is not one of ours, or something is missing from it (address, key, or the machine\'s TLS fingerprint). If the machine listens on 0.0.0.0, change it to the specific address.
There is an armed order waiting
Your fingerprint authorises it. No need to type the code.
This phone cannot sign: answer with %1$s.
Your fingerprint authorises this order and only this one.
Cancelled. The order stays armed until it expires.
The system did not return the signature; nothing was confirmed.
I could not sign the confirmation: %1$s
This phone cannot sign confirmations (no biometric enrolled, or no usable Keystore). Use the code.
Pair this phone with %1$s:%2$d\n\nand store the key and TLS fingerprint that came with the order.
Change the machine\'s address to %1$s:%2$d\n\nThe key and the pairing itself are untouched.
\n\nThis arrived in the intent that opened the app. If you did not just do this from a PC, say no.
Not paired — the machine and the key are missing
⚠️ The machine says this is NOT the phone it was paired with. If you did not re-pair it, somebody else has the pairing key.
no connection — cannot send it yet
no connection — the photo did not go out
no connection — I could not confirm

This pairing predates TLS on the channel and has no fingerprint for the machine stored.\n\nScan the QR again: I will not connect without being able to check that the thing answering is your machine and not another.
I could not connect to %1$s:%2$d.\n\nThis is a direct connection: there is no relay. Check that you are on the same network as the machine, or that the VPN is up.
I could not establish TLS with %1$s:%2$d.\n\n%3$s
This phone offers neither TLS 1.2 nor 1.3. It is too old to talk to the machine safely.

The machine's key is not the one you saved when pairing.

Expected %1$s
and got %2$s.

Either the daemon was reinstalled (and you need to pair again), or somebody is answering in its place.

The frame did not authenticate.\n\nAlmost always this means the pairing key does not match the machine\'s. If the machine uses ChaCha20-Poly1305 (a CPU with no hardware AES), this phone needs Android 9 or later.
